# Boker (bot poker): build the game

Boker is a poker game played in one self-contained HTML file (inline CSS and JS, no network), opened in any browser on desktop or phone. Play chips only, never real money.

## Table
- deAIler (dealer): shuffles, deals, burns before flop/turn/river, posts blinds/antes, runs pot and side pots, returns uncalled bets; never plays.
- JudgAIe (referee): enforces rules, blocks out-of-turn or illegal actions (e.g. check facing a bet, under-min raise bumped to min, drawing more than 3), shows a ruling line, evaluates showdown.
- Me: the human seat; own cards face up, NPC cards face down until showdown.
- 3 NPCs: random first names each game (mix of male and female, no duplicates), each with a random personality.
- Each player starts with $1,250 ($5,000 total).

## Games (dealer's choice)
The button rotates; whoever holds it picks the game for that hand. Playable: Texas Hold'em (no-limit, blinds $10/$20) and Five-Card Draw (no-limit, $10 ante, discard up to 3). Omaha, Seven-Card Stud and Razz show as coming soon. NPCs pick a game according to personality.

## NPC personalities (coded rules, no AI API)
Rock/Nit, TAG, LAG, Maniac, Calling Station, Weak-Tight, Shark (adapts to opponents' observed fold and raise rates, including Me), Fish, GTO (balanced, pot-odds mixed strategy). Each has its own emoji, subtitle, betting strategy and table-talk lines; NPCs talk to everyone. NPCs estimate hand strength only from their own cards plus public cards (no cheating). Cap raises per betting round so raise wars end.

## UI and sound
Seats with chips, bet, last action, turn marker, dealer button; community cards and pot in the middle; fold, check/call, bet/raise with slider and half-pot/pot/max shortcuts; table-talk and dealer log; referee ruling line; busted players marked OUT; game-over screen with Play again. A card snap sound per card dealt, synthesized with the Web Audio API, starting after the first tap, with a mute toggle. Responsive layout for phones.

## Steps
1. Hand the build to a background worker with this spec; save the file in the workspace.
2. Require a Node test script: hand evaluator on known hands (wheel, kickers, ties, best of 7), referee checks, and at least 1,000 simulated NPC-only hands with legal actions only and the chip total constant.
3. Send the HTML file to the owner as an attachment and say what was and wasn't tested in a browser.
4. Phones may not open local HTML files well; offer to host it as a web page (e.g. GitHub Pages).

# Getting started with Boker

Say in one line: I build and run Boker, a poker game you play in your browser against three bot opponents with their own personalities, dealt by deAIler and refereed by JudgAIe. Play chips only.

Ask one at a time:
1. What should I call you at the table? (default: Me)
2. Will you mostly play on a computer or a phone?
3. Any changes before I build it: starting chips (default $1,250 each), blinds, or which games to include?

Then save the answers as memories, run the boker-build skill with them, and send the game file. If they play on a phone, offer to host it as a web page.
